title: Returned Payments and the Months of a Ridgeline Home Improvement Financing Hardship Deferral
content:
*Payments risk guidance, Ridgeline Home Improvement Financing.*

**Rule.** On an account whose plan carries no promotion (a fixed-rate or low-payment plan), payments returned unpaid in the twelve months before the grant adjust the months of a hardship deferral: two or more take two months away; exactly one takes a month away; none, on an account still enrolled in autopay, adds a month; anything else leaves the months alone. The adjustment is added to the months asked on the request, and the months granted are never more than the months asked nor below zero.

**Q. Which returns are counted?**
A. The payments returned unpaid by the bank on that financing account, dated in the twelve months before the day the deferral is granted.

**Q. What does each count do?**

| Payments returned unpaid in the 12 months | Enrolled in autopay at the grant | Adjustment |
|---|---|---|
| 2 or more | Either | Less 2 months |
| Exactly 1 | Either | Less 1 month |
| None | Yes | Plus 1 month |
| None | No | None |

**Q. Where is the line between one and two?**
A. A count of 2 is the returned limit and takes two months away; a count of 1 takes one month away.

**Q. Hypothetical example.** A request asks for 2 months; one payment was returned eight months before the grant: 2 less 1 gives 1 month. Had the return been fourteen months before the grant, it would fall outside the twelve months, and an account still enrolled in autopay would take plus 1, held at the 2 months asked.
